title: He Was Just a Shepherd… Until God Spoke His Name
paragraphs:
He Was Just a Shepherd… Until God Spoke His Name
The Scandal of Being Unqualified and the Grace That Turns Nobodies into Prophets
There are callings that make sense… and then there are the kind that feel almost offensive.

Because if we’re honest, when we picture a prophet, we imagine someone trained, polished, chosen early, prepared for the spotlight. Someone who looks the part. Sounds the part. Lives somewhere close to power, influence, and religious prestige.
But Amos?

Amos was dirt under the fingernails.
Amos smelled like sheep.
Amos was unnoticed… until heaven interrupted his ordinary.
And maybe that’s why this story hits harder than most.
Because it exposes something we don’t like to admit—God doesn’t need our qualifications… He looks for our surrender.
Amos himself didn’t pretend otherwise. He said it plainly in Amos 7:14:
“I was no prophet, neither was I a prophet’s son; but I was an herdman, and a gatherer of sycomore fruit…”
In Hebrew, the word he uses for shepherd is “בּוֹקֵר” (bōqēr)—not a royal shepherd, not a poetic figure, but a simple cattle herder. A laborer. A nobody in the eyes of society.
And yet… that’s exactly where God went.

Not to the palace.
Not to the academy.
Not to the religious elite.
God walked into the fields… and called a man who didn’t even think he belonged in the conversation.
Let that settle in you.
Because some of you have already disqualified yourselves from what God is trying to do in your life.

You think your past is too messy.
Your voice too small.
Your knowledge too limited.
Your life too ordinary.
But Amos didn’t upgrade himself into a prophet.
God rewrote him into one.
And when God calls, He doesn’t ask for permission from your insecurity.
The calling of Amos wasn’t comfortable either. God didn’t lift him up just to celebrate him. He sent him into confrontation.
Into a nation that had grown spiritually numb. Into a people who performed religion but abandoned righteousness.
The message was heavy. Unpopular. Dangerous.
In Amos 5:24, God speaks through him:
“But let judgment run down as waters, and righteousness as a mighty stream.”
In Hebrew, “justice” is “מִשְׁפָּט” (mishpat)—not just fairness, but divine order restored. And “righteousness,” “צְדָקָה” (tsedaqah)—a life aligned with God’s heart, not just outward behavior.
God wasn’t impressed with their rituals.
He wanted their hearts back.
And Amos… the shepherd… became the voice.
This is where it gets uncomfortable.
Because we love the idea of being chosen… but we hesitate when we realize what that calling might demand.

Amos had no platform.
No following.
No safety net.
Just obedience.
And obedience will cost you something.

It might cost your comfort.
Your reputation.
Your relationships.
Your plans.
But here’s the truth most people avoid:
The life you’re trying to protect might be the very thing keeping you from becoming who God called you to be.
And that’s the scandal.
God doesn’t just call the prepared… He prepares the called.
Even when they’re standing in a field, holding nothing but a shepherd’s staff.
Even when they feel like imposters.
Even when they don’t see it yet.
If you’ve ever felt like you’re too far behind, too broken, too unseen, too unqualified…
You are standing exactly where Amos stood.
And that means this might be your moment.

Not because you’re ready…
But because God is.
Be honest for a second…
Have you been running from something you know God is asking you to step into?
Have you been hiding behind “I’m not ready” when deep down, you know it’s really fear?
Let that be your first step out of silence.
And if you feel like your faith has been weak, inconsistent, or tired lately…
There’s something powerful about saying it out loud.
Remind them that heaven still calls shepherds.
And if you want to stay rooted in truth like this daily—real Scripture, real conviction, real transformation—follow closely.
Not for content… but for alignment.
Because following truth keeps you from drifting back into comfortable lies.
And if you’re serious about growing deeper in Jesus Christ—not surface-level faith, but real discipleship, healing, accountability—there’s more waiting for you.
If God is using this to stir something in you… don’t ignore it.
Support what is feeding your spirit.
Because when you help spread truth, you’re not just supporting content—you’re participating in someone else’s encounter with God.
Because glorifying God isn’t passive… it moves, it shares, it multiplies.
And maybe… just maybe…
The next “Amos” is someone reading this right now, thinking they’re still just a shepherd.
But heaven has already said your name.
And once God speaks… ordinary is no longer your identity.
You were never just what you did… you are who He calls you to become.
